call_points.text: Pricing is guided by holding EBITDA margin at 21-24%, with further action if raw material or forex moves adversely.
Management expects commodity and feedstock inflation to be more visible in Q3.
Two price increases between January and June, with Q2 pricing action in low double digits.
Q2 benefited from consuming older low-cost inventory; management declined to quantify the gain.
Group 3 base oil prices are elevated, impacted by the Middle East crisis.
Industrial business is about 15% of overall business and growing faster than the rest.
Capex runs about ₹100 Cr a year, split between plants and market visibility.
Data centre cooling fluids: products ready for both immersion and direct-to-chip, some trials converted to business but not material yet.
Silvassa plant shut for a couple of days in July after heavy rain; now back at Q2 peak levels with no impact.
Analyst pressed on volume numbers; management said it does not share specific volumes, though the analyst said it was shared on earlier calls.
BP's divestment of 65% of global Castrol to Stonepeak is progressing; open offer timing depends on deal closure.
Volume growth for the quarter stood at 7% to 8% on a year-on-year basis.
The company follows a 60-day hedging policy covering its foreign currency exposure on imported raw materials.
Rural portfolio continues to grow at high double-digit rates with distribution expanded across 40,000 outlets.

penalties.authority: Registrar of Companies, Mumbai, (ROC) Ministry of Corporate Affairs
penalties.details: The ROC issued a Show Cause Notice (SCN) for e-adjudication of default under Section 450 read with Section 454 of the Companies Act, 2013, in connection with the filing of Form MR-2 for the appointment of the Whole-time Director, which could not be completed within the prescribed timeline due to technical issues faced with the MCA website and the process for filing of MR-2. The Company had to acknowledge the facts stated in SCN and proceed with the adjudication given there was no other recourse to process Form MR-2 as stated by MCA in their letter to the Company and ROC. Accordingly, the ROC passed an adjudication order imposing penalty on the Company and its officers in default. The Company and its officers duly complied with the order within the prescribed timelines, and Form INC-28 filed in this regard has been approved by the ROC. Form MR-2 would be processed in due course by MCA as the adjudication process as directed by MCA has been completed successfully.
penalties.impact: No impact on the financial, operation or other activities of the Company

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had received demand orders from the Maharashtra Sales Tax Department amounting to INR 4131.25 Crores in relation to the movement of goods from its Plant/Warehouses in Maharashtra to CFAs in other states, which the department claims were inter-state sales. The Company has disputed this demand stating that the goods were not moved under pre-existing orders from other states and that its tax payment methodology is legally supported. The Company has received favorable orders from the MVAT Tribunal [previously Maharashtra Sales Tax Tribunal (MSTT)] for the periods 2007-08, 2010-11 to 2015-16 and 2017-18, while the department has appealed against the said orders before CESTAT. Thus considering the favorable orders from MVAT Tribunal and based on the legal advice the Company has not made any provision in the books for the financial year ended 31st Mar 2025 and the possibility of outflow of resources embodying economic benefits is considered to be remote. Further, the Company has received favourable order on 11 July 2025 from CESTAT for the period 2007-08 to 2015-16 and 2017-18 (9 out of 10 years). For the year 2016-17, Maharashtra Sales Tax Department has not contested the order of MVAT Tribunal. Accordingly, litigation for the aforementioned years is now being treated as closed.
tax_litigation.status: The Company has received intimation that the Maharashtra Sales Tax Department has filed an appeal for the balance period FY 2016-17 before Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT).The appeal has been filed with an application for condonation of delay and hearing is scheduled on 31 July 2026.

tax_litigation.status: The Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) has dismissed Maharashtra Sales Tax Department appeal dated 31 July 2026 for condonation of delay.
